description.narrative: Pacific Women Lead is Australia's leading regional investment in gender equality in the Pacific. This program builds on Pacific Women Shaping Pacific Development and follows locally-led development principles. The program focusses on strengthening gender equality throughout the Pacific region through focussing on women's leadership and rights, including safety, health, economic empowerment and responding to and preventing family and gender-based violence. Pacific Women Lead also focusses on strengthening regional architecture and increasing effectiveness of regional gender equality efforts through working with SPC, UN agencies, and civil society, specifically Pacific Women's organisations.

title.narrative: Pacific Women Lead Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Framework
Pacific Women Lead Annual Progress Report (2021-2023)

description.narrative: Australia is supporting the UN Women’s Markets for Change (M4C) program, in partnership with the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), to improve the socioeconomic security of women market vendors in Fiji, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands and Samoa. Under the program, a virtual mentoring program was implemented in Fiji, reaching 440 women vendors. In Samoa, financial management training sessions were conducted in collaboration with the Samoa Business Hub for 102 women vendors, with 100 vendors receiving tablet devices to strengthen business and data management. In Solomon Islands, UNDP provided specialised financial and business management training for 100 women vendors to improve their socioeconomic security. In Vanuatu, a total of 116 market vendors received Money Minded Training by ANZ Bank. Post-activity interviews indicated improvements in participants’ socioeconomic stability, including increased income, savings and access to financial resources such as loans and investments. Approximately 25 per cent of vendors demonstrated financial self-reliance, actively engaging with gender-inclusive social and financial services.

In 2023/2024, the Pacific Feminist Fund (PFF) launched its first grant round targeting the North Pacific. Using AIR Partnership funds, PFF issued grants to grassroots women’s rights organisations in the Federated States of Micronesia, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Nauru, Palau, and Tuvalu.

In 2024, UNDP partnered with Solomon Islands National Provident Fund, ANZ Bank, and Telekom to deliver targeted financial literacy and business management training to 393 women market vendors. These sessions covered assertiveness, goal setting, cash flow, and risk forecasting—critical tools for small business success. Additionally, 317 women accessed tailored financial products through the YouSave initiative, while 300 vendors registered SIM cards to support digital transactions. Two women vendors even became Telekom agents, enhancing market access to financial services. This coordinated approach boosted vendor resilience, with 35% of 550 assessed vendors demonstrating financial self-reliance and improved economic stability.

In 2024, the SPC Women in Leadership (WIL) program significantly advanced institutional accountability by embedding gender equality across SPC's governance systems. A major achievement was the endorsement of SPC’s Domestic Violence Standard Operating Procedures (DV SOPs), the first of its kind within a CROP agency. These SOPs were accompanied by a recruitment plan for Gender and GBV Advisers and the appointment of Wellbeing Focal Points across SPC campuses. This institutional reform, backed by senior leadership, reflects strong alignment with regional commitments and ensures safer, more inclusive workplaces. These changes position SPC as a model for other regional government institutions.

Pacific Women Lead at SPC funded rapid reviews of the only crisis centres in RMI and FSM—Weto In Mour (WIM) and Tongen Inepwineu Counseling Center (TICC). These reviews became transformative moments, empowering centre staff through participatory evaluation methods. Staff built skills in data collection, analysis, and strategic planning, leading to centre-owned design documents for future services. Survivors increasingly expressed comfort engaging with the centres, particularly valuing WIM’s female counsellors. The process shifted crisis centre teams from service delivery to active leadership in system reform, ensuring survivors’ voices are central to design and delivery.

Technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV) is endemic in the Pacific, perpetrated through technology including abusive text messaging, image-based abuse through social media, or controlling access to devices. With Australian funding under the Pacific Women Lead program, The Pacific Community (SPC) held the inaugural eSafety Symposium, collaborating with Australia’s eSafety Commissioner, the University of the South Pacific (USP) and Pacific Island Forum Secretariat (PIFS). ‍ 130 participants from the region attended, with 45 guest speakers, including five adolescent girls. The eSafety Symposium allowed for the first Pacific-style talanoa and storytelling, generating data and insights for addressing TFGBV. ‍ As a result, the region’s first TFGBV Priorities Document was developed and endorsed, clarifying priorities by country. Following the event, the Solomon Islands’ delegation arranged for TFGBV Training for Frontline Workers to be delivered in-country within two months, with Fiji following in December 2023. The pilot training was launched during the symposium by Australia’s eSafety Commissioner.

The Pacific Community (SPC) is strengthening and embedding gender approaches across SPC operations including a corporate Women in Leadership (WIL) initiative and implementing a Gender Equality Flagship program to mainstream gender equality into SPC’s core business model across all its divisions. The WIL program within SPC is the first institutional investment by a Council of Regional Organisations (CROP) agency focussed on improving governance and effectiveness through strengthening women’s leadership, gender equality and inclusion. SPC has introduced structural reforms to transform organisational culture and improve opportunities for women within the organisation including improved accountability mechanisms, policies and procedures. SPC’s senior leadership team is driving the implementation of the recommendations from the SPC 2022 Leadership Audit to mainstream gender equality and inclusion within SPC (and more broadly in other regional organisations through the CROP Women of the Wave Network) positioning SPC as a regional leader in inclusion and diversity in the workplace.

The We Rise Coalition is a partnership between Pacific feminist organisations working to advance gender equality and the human rights of women (including women with disabilities) and people of diverse sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, and sexual characteristics. It brings together seven Pacific feminist organisations to amplify Pacific women’s leadership and voice to advance gender equality through organisational strengthening, movement building, and policy and institutional reform. ‍ In 2023, the We Rise Coalition successfully co-facilitated the 3rd Pacific Feminist Forum. Over 150 feminists from 17 Pacific countries came together to jointly strategise on advancing gender equality in the Pacific. In the context of increasing resistance to gender equality globally, the Pacific Feminist Forum is an important collective space for feminist activists to collaborate and create positive change. The Pacific Feminist Forum Outcomes Statement sets out an advocacy roadmap to guide the work of Pacific feminist organisations nationally, regionally and globally.

UN Women’s Markets for Change with the United Nations Development Program improved the socioeconomic security of women market vendors (WMVs) in Fiji and Vanuatu. 668 rural WMVs reported improvements in Fiji and 34 in Vanuatu. UNDP worked with financial institutions to offer training to build awareness and access to financial services. 40 percent of WMV training participants in Fiji reported increased income, savings or financial capital and greater agency in financial decision-making. 20 per cent of WMVs in Vanuatu reported improved business, record keeping and financial skills, including the ability to start and maintain savings, and improved digital literacy.

We Rise Coalition partner Voice for Change (VfC) supported 60 survivors of gender-based violence with counselling, medical and legal support. This enabled survivors to register cases with local village courts resulting in the provision of restraining orders and financial compensation to survivors VfC consulted with the health and education sector, village courts, police, and community organisations to discuss the interlinkages between the court system and police response and to map referral pathways for survivors. VfC advocacy, service provision and awareness raising, has increased the number of survivors taking legal action under the Domestic Violence Act and court orders issued
